title: Oyatie Cloud source-backed hyperscaler parity taxonomy and honest nonclaim matrix
purpose: Defines the backend/cloud-native/hyperscaler category taxonomy that Oyatie Cloud must eventually satisfy for AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and OCI parity claims. This artifact is a claim-control matrix: it maps official provider/Kubernetes/CNCF evidence to Oyatie target categories while explicitly blocking unsupported maturity, production, and feature-parity claims.

included: mapping to remaining ultragoal implementation goals
excluded: provider account access or live provisioning

official_source_evidence.evidence_use: AWS publishes a broad global cloud services catalog plus Marketplace/global-infrastructure context; used as the AWS catalog/category baseline.
AWS EC2 evidence for VM compute, capacity elasticity, instance families, regional/AZ placement, and compute SLA/availability expectations.
AWS EKS evidence for managed Kubernetes as a core hyperscaler container service.
AWS S3 evidence for object storage category coverage.
AWS IAM evidence for identity/access policy category coverage.
AWS Lambda evidence for functions/serverless compute category coverage.
AWS RDS evidence for managed relational database category coverage.
Google Cloud official product catalog; used for Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, operations, security/identity, marketplace, and product launch-stage expectations.
Azure official product catalog; used for VMs, AKS, Functions, storage, databases, networking, security, observability, cost management, and Marketplace category coverage.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure official cloud page; used for OCI services, regions, free-tier core services, containers/functions, networking, databases, security, observability, and cost/governance categories.
Kubernetes official concepts; used to ground the Kubernetes-native/declarative control-plane shape and to avoid claiming Kubernetes solves logging/monitoring/config-management by itself.

CNCF cloud native definition v1.1; used for the cloud-native attributes: secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable, observable, loosely coupled, automation-friendly, declarative APIs, multi-tenancy, serverless, containers, service meshes, microservices, and immutable infrastructure.
AWS VPC evidence for virtual networking, resource placement, connectivity, and security boundaries.
AWS Route 53 evidence for DNS, routing policy, health checking, and DNS firewall networking coverage.
AWS CloudWatch evidence for metrics, logs, traces, infrastructure/application observability, and OpenTelemetry-compatible operations.
AWS KMS evidence for key management and cryptographic control coverage.
AWS Budgets evidence for cost planning, budget thresholds, alerts/actions, and usage governance.
AWS Cost Explorer evidence for cost and usage analytics and forecast coverage.
AWS Marketplace evidence for partner/ISV product catalog and delivery method coverage.
AWS Security Hub evidence for security posture and guardrail coverage.

category_taxonomy.name: Identity, access, tenancy, and policy control plane
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Tenant/account/project-scoped principals, roles, policy bindings, workload identity, policy simulation/preview, audit trail, and least-privilege enforcement.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Virtual machine compute and fleet lifecycle
category_taxonomy.target_capability: ORN-addressed VM instances, images, machine shapes, lifecycle state transitions, placement/region/cell metadata, quotas, billing meters, idempotent operations, and cancellation semantics.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Managed Kubernetes and container runtime surface
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Kubernetes-native cluster, node pool, workload identity, network/storage integration, upgrade policy, conformance evidence, tenant isolation, and cluster operations.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim
Kubernetes conformance or explicit non-conformance evidence

category_taxonomy.name: Functions/serverless and event-driven compute
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Declarative function/container execution resource with event sources, workload identity, cold-start/resource limits, logs/traces, quota/billing, and rollback semantics.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Object, block, file, snapshot, and retention storage
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Buckets, block volumes, file shares, snapshots, backup/retention policies, encryption metadata, lifecycle states, quotas, billing meters, and durability evidence.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Virtual networking, DNS, load balancing, edge, and connectivity
category_taxonomy.target_capability: VPC/VCN/VNet-equivalent networks, subnets, routes, security groups/firewalls, DNS zones/records, load balancers, private endpoints, gateways, and edge policy metadata.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Managed databases, data services, analytics, and migration
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Declarative database/data resources with engine/version metadata, backup/restore, replication, connection/security policy, quotas, billing meters, audit events, and lifecycle operations.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Key management, secrets, confidential data, and cryptographic controls
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Key rings, keys, key versions, secret references, secret mount policy, rotation/disable/destroy state, envelope encryption metadata, audit events, and no raw secret material in control-plane state.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Observability, logging, tracing, operations, status, and support evidence
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Per-resource metrics/logs/traces, audit/control-plane events, SLO tier metadata, burn-rate evidence, health/status surfaces, incident/drill records, and support/runbook metadata.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Billing, metering, FinOps, budgets, quotas, and cost governance
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Usage meters, rated line items, quotas/service limits, budgets, cost allocation, forecast/alert hooks, deletion-retention cost effects, and tenant/account/project cost scoping.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Marketplace, partner/ISV, images, templates, and solution catalog
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Curated image/template/catalog resource model with provenance, license/terms, vulnerability/compliance metadata, rollout/rollback controls, billing/metering attachments, and tenant eligibility policy.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Security posture, threat detection, guardrails, WAF/firewall, compliance, and safety gates
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Policy packs, posture findings, threat/abuse indicators, guardrails, security zones, WAF/firewall rules, compliance evidence, and irreversible-action safety barriers.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim

category_taxonomy.name: Cloud-native/Kubernetes-native platform contract
category_taxonomy.target_capability: Vendor-neutral declarative APIs, loosely coupled services, multi-tenancy, automation, resilience, manageability, sustainability, observability, containers/Kubernetes, serverless, service mesh, immutable infrastructure, and explicit boundaries for what Kubernetes does not provide.
required_evidence: targeted tests plus governance gate evidence
measured operational evidence before production claim
observability explicitly outside Kubernetes core where applicable

can_claim_now.claim: Oyatie Cloud now has a source-backed, machine-readable target taxonomy for core backend hyperscaler categories.
can_claim_now.limits: Target taxonomy only; runtime equivalence and operational launch language remain blocked in cannot_claim_yet and nonclaims.

can_claim_now.claim: Existing Oyatie Cloud specs already frame cloud-* resources as ORN-addressed, quota/billing/audit/lifecycle/SLO/deletion-retention facets.
can_claim_now.limits: Those specs are Proposed-target and metadata-only until implementation and measured operations evidence exist.

can_claim_now.claim: The plan intentionally uses strict separation and pure dogfood controls for future CI/evidence work.
evidence: user directive in active ultragoal brief
can_claim_now.limits: The actual CI lane reconciliation is deferred to G007.

cannot_claim_yet.claim: Same feature parity with AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or OCI.
blocked_by: no implemented catalog expansion for every category
hyperscaler gates are not all green
quality evidence kits are not measured

cannot_claim_yet.claim: Production-ready cloud substrate or tenant/product workload readiness.
Kubernetes conformance, managed-Kubernetes service readiness, or cluster upgrade/failover readiness.
Public SLA/SLO availability for cloud resources.

nonclaims.replacement_statement: Oyatie Cloud has a target taxonomy and pending gate-backed implementation/evidence work.

nonclaims.blocked_statement: Oyatie Cloud has the same feature parity as AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or OCI.
nonclaims.replacement_statement: This taxonomy defines the parity categories and required evidence before such a claim can be evaluated.
Production readiness requires measured quality kits, SLO evidence, CI evidence, and final reviews.

nonclaims.blocked_statement: Tenant or product workloads can be safely migrated onto Oyatie Cloud.
nonclaims.replacement_statement: Workload migration remains blocked until the cloud substrate, observability, security, and rollout evidence are green.

nonclaims.blocked_statement: Oyatie Cloud offers public SLA/SLO guarantees.
nonclaims.replacement_statement: SLO/SLA language requires measured burn-rate and incident evidence plus an approved support/status process.

nonclaims.blocked_statement: Oyatie Cloud provisions real cloud resources across providers.
nonclaims.replacement_statement: This lane remains local/self-hosted/dogfood; live provider apply/provisioning is explicitly excluded.

doubt_driven_review.challenge: A broad taxonomy could be mistaken for product parity.
doubt_driven_review.resolution: Every category carries required evidence, local claim status, and explicit cannot-claim-yet rows. Validator locks Proposed-target status and required nonclaims.
doubt_driven_review.residual_risk: Official provider catalogs change; source refresh must occur before future parity claims or public documentation.

Compute and observability are discoverable as target/backlog vocabulary with explicit non-claims until runtime, provisioning, and measured SLO evidence gates are green.
